_comment: Block manifest graded by `klt signoff --manifest`. See README.md for the regeneration command and the pin.

ITEM 5 (full corner verification vs a ratified spec), added by issue #30. Five `klt sim` envelopes, one per row family, each naming the spec/target-spec.md row ids it covers; `spec_rows.5` declares the FULL row set, so a row no envelope covers is visible in the report instead of being silently absent.

The declared row set is spec/target-spec.md's ELECTRICAL rows -- the rows whose Binding-conditions column is the §PVT grid. The Area and Signoff rows of that table are deliberately NOT declared here: their binding conditions are a layout cell and the DRC/LVS/ERC decks, which T1 items 2, 3 and 4 grade. Declaring them under item 5 would make a layout artifact a corner-verification gap.

Item 5 is UNMET on purpose. Three declared rows are gaps: the untrimmed-line 3-sigma row, the trimmed-line row and the Trim row. The first needs a device-mismatch Monte Carlo reduction (issue #31), which a corner matrix cannot express and which T1 item 6 grades; the other two need a trim network that does not exist in this design yet. Naming a narrower row set would have rendered item 5 `met` by leaving the block's unevidenced accuracy rows out of the declaration, which is exactly the relaxation CLAUDE.md forbids.

The Supply row is declared as a gap rather than covered because spec/target-spec.md states it is met BY CONSTRUCTION (HV device rating, inherited) and not by a result: every cited envelope did run the ratified 2.97/3.30/3.63 V axis, but no measurement in them establishes the row, and asserting coverage from a supply value the request itself set would be circular.

Each cited envelope carries `spec_row` tags on its graded measurements, so `klt signoff` DERIVES this coverage from the envelopes (`row_coverage.row_sources` reads `derived`) instead of taking the manifest's word for it.

5.gap: device-mismatch Monte Carlo reduction (3 sigma over N >= 300 samples per corner point) that a klt sim corner matrix cannot express; its bench does not exist yet (issue #31), and T1 item 6 is where the statistical claim is graded
